highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude Opus 5, their most capable model yet, featuring a 1M token context window and a fast mode priced at $10/$50 per million tokens. This is a significant upgrade for developers who need to process large codebases or long documents in a single session. Claude Opus 5 is now the default Opus model in Claude Code as of v2.1.219.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219 Released
highlights.summary: This release adds Claude Opus 5 as the default Opus model and introduces `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist`, a new setting that automatically denies network access to non-allowlisted hosts in sandboxed commands without prompting. The `DirectoryAdded` hook is also new, giving developers more control over automation triggers. If you use sandboxing for security, update now to take advantage of stricter network controls.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218 Released
highlights.summary: The `/code-review` slash command now runs as a background subagent, meaning it no longer clutters your main conversation thread and correctly targets stacked slash commands for review. This makes iterative code review much cleaner, especially when chaining multiple commands together. Screen-reader accessibility also improved with announcements for deleted text.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.216 Released
highlights.summary: A critical performance fix lands in this release: long sessions were suffering multi-second stalls due to message normalization costs growing quadratically with the number of turns — this is now resolved. A new `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` setting lets you skip filesystem isolation while still controlling network egress, giving you more granular sandbox configuration. If you've noticed slowdowns in lengthy Claude Code sessions, updating to this version should help significantly.

highlights.title: Show HN: A local merge queue for parallel Claude Code agents
highlights.summary: A developer running 4-5 parallel Claude Code agents and pushing up to 90 commits a day on an 8GB MacBook Air built a local merge queue to prevent agents from colliding when they try to build, test, and run dev servers simultaneously. This tool serializes agent operations so they don't overwhelm limited hardware or burn unnecessary CI minutes. If you're experimenting with multi-agent workflows, this is a practical solution to a real bottleneck.

highlights.title: Show HN: Claude-account – switch Claude Code accounts without logging in again
highlights.summary: This small CLI tool lets you manage multiple Claude Code accounts (e.g., work and personal) and switch between them instantly without going through the full login flow each time. Commands are simple: `claude account add <name>` and `claude account use <name>`. A handy quality-of-life tool if you frequently context-switch between different Claude Code subscriptions or API keys.

highlights.title: How Does Claude Code Actually Work? Let's Make Our Own
highlights.summary: This YouTube video digs into the internals of Claude Code by walking through building a simplified version from scratch, giving you a deeper understanding of how the tool orchestrates file edits, tool calls, and conversation context. Understanding the underlying mechanics helps you write better prompts and debug unexpected behavior. Recommended for developers who want to go beyond surface-level usage.

highlights.title: Claude Code Tutorial for Non-Coders
highlights.summary: This beginner-friendly video tutorial walks non-developers through using Claude Code to build and modify projects without prior programming experience. It covers the basics of issuing prompts, reviewing changes, and iterating on results in plain language. A great starting point if you're new to AI coding tools and want a gentle introduction.

tips_of_the_day: Use `/code-review` as a background subagent (v2.1.218+) to keep your main conversation clean — stack it after other slash commands and it will correctly target the latest changes without polluting your chat history.

If you're running parallel Claude Code agents on a low-RAM machine, serialize their build and test steps rather than letting them run concurrently — even a simple file-based lock mechanism can prevent OOM crashes and wasted work.

Take advantage of `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` (v2.1.219+) to harden your Claude Code sandbox: define exactly which hosts sandboxed commands can reach and everything else is silently denied, reducing accidental data exfiltration risks during automated tasks.
